references.text: Earlier in the chapter, it is described how the Egyptians, with horses, chariots, and riders, pursued the Israelites, which directly leads to this pursuit into the sea.
God predicts that he will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will pursue the Israelites into the sea, which is fulfilled in this verse.
Describes the consequence of the Egyptians' pursuit into the sea—the water returned and covered the chariots, riders, and the entire army of Pharaoh.
Moses' song celebrates how horse and rider were cast into the sea, a poetic reference to the event described in 14:23.
The song describes how Pharaoh's chariots and army were cast into the sea, and his chosen officers sank in the Sea of Reeds.
A summary of how Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and riders went into the sea, and the Lord caused the water to return over them.
The psalm praises God for shaking Pharaoh and his army in the Sea of Reeds, a reference to the Egyptians' destruction after the pursuit.
Hebrews mentions how the Israelites passed through the Red Sea on dry ground, while the Egyptians drowned when they attempted the same—a direct reference to this event.
A historical summary in Joshua's speech confirms and interprets the event from Exodus as proof of God's salvation.
Prophetic precondition (God hardens the heart) explains the cause of the actual event in v.23.
Poetic summary of the same event, confirming that the pursuit ended in God's judgment.
Deuteronomic reflection interpreting the event as lasting proof of God's salvation and judgment.
